title: Global Warming
question: How is the Earth’s climate changing, what role do people play, and what should the country do about it?
summary: A page about the science, the impacts, and the policy choices — kept separate, so a disagreement about one of them is not treated as a disagreement about all three.
sourceNote: Further reading only. This outline does not take facts from these pages yet. When the full page is written, government or other primary sources will be cited first, and the Just Facts page will stay linked as further reading. The wording on this site will stay original. No statistics are included here.

paragraphs: This section will explain, in everyday words, what people mean by global warming and the greenhouse effect, and it will keep the science, the impacts, and the policy choices from getting mashed into one claim.
No statistics will be added until they are checked against primary sources.

This section will separate arguments about what the measurements show, arguments about how bad the effects may be, and arguments about what the government should require. Those are related, and they are not the same fight.

sides.intro: Each column will hold one side’s strongest fair case, in plain language and at similar length. Neither case is written yet.

a.title: One side’s strongest case
paragraphs: This column will give the strongest fair case for one view, using checked facts. It will not use insults, and it is not written yet.

b.title: The other side’s strongest case
paragraphs: This column will give the strongest fair case for the other view, under the same rules. It is not written yet.

This section will look for ground that does not depend on pretending the science fight and the policy fight are identical. Shared goals might include wanting honest measurements and wanting to avoid waste.

items: The questions will ask what would count as good evidence, and what a fair policy would still have to decide even if the measurements were not in dispute.

sources.title: U.S. Environmental Protection Agency: Climate Change Indicators
sources.note: An official indicator set this page will read before any climate number is added. NASA’s climate pages will be checked too. Nothing is copied here yet.
